institutionName: Hong Kong University of Science and Technology

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: That the whether was good at all times - And it do be like that in Hong Kong, trust me

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: You should go! Hong Kong is a great place to study if you love a vibrant city and beautiful nature and amazing beaches. Might be the best choice of my life.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The school is a very respectable school in asia, and they are used to exchange students, also from Denmark. There will be no issues for you to figure out all the logistics, cause they gonna help you with all the practical stuff

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Everything that I need and plenty of reminders

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: As undergrad exchange student you are promised a place to live on campus, which was very cheap

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: You ate at the school cantins, there are plenty of options, even macy d's, Starbucks and subway. A lot of other stuff, but hardly any cooking facilities

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: It's not glamoures, but you are hardly ever in your room, because of all the activities that are available at the school. Everything from tennis to judo classes. Don't spend your time in a room anyways.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: you got everything sent though mail, very easy

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: All the help you needed, they always responded within a day.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very successful, got everything that I wanted, even tho I am a social science student, I got all the business classes that I wanted

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Nothing to worry about, you gonna figure it out. if in doubt, just ask

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The courses I took was very easy. HKUST is also called University of Stress and Tension in Hong Kong by the locals. You need to take classes that you know are easy, because they do have some very hard ones at the school. I chose easy, cause I just wanted to chill and have fun. I do enough school at KU. But you also have a 2 week add and drop period, so you gonna figure it out.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Very different, a lot more including. Grades not only based on one exam, but on plenty of other stuff as well

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: -negotiations, Entrepreneurship and Innovation, international manament and intermediate investment

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The same as me, very easy to pass. Negotiations was very fun actually and good if you are bad at negotiation

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: It is not unexpected, but I travelled a lot and partied a lot, which is expensive. Hong Kong I very central in asia, and has very cheap flights out. This resulted in me traveling 8 different countries while I was there, this because a pretty big cost. But it is possible to do the exchange very cheap. I would however recommend to spend it all if possible, the experience wouldn't be as nice if I didn't spend the money I did. Very fun experience.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: tickets out of Hong Kong very cheap - but the drinks at the clubs were pretty expensive, so hit the local 7/11

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Anything you wanted to do was free at the school - Trust me

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There were plenty of things to do, just be open to it.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Do the sports activities there, more or less like a university like in the states, where everything is at campus

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Go travel, all countries are 2-3 hours away from Hong Kong. Be smart with your classes, put all classes Tuesday-thursdag. Gives you 5 days off and plenty of time for weekend trips away

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: little more difficult, cause their culture is very different. However all the exchange students live on campus, so you will meet plenty of people that you can have blast with. I hung out a lot with Danes but could also have been with a lot of other nationalities. I just choose this.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Be open, be like people from Jutland, not like the people from copenhagen

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The cantonese people shout a lot

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Their dumplings, to die fore

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Go! you gonna have so much fun. Its gonna be a hell to plan exchange, but you will forget all about that stuff once you are there - not gonna regret a single thing. 
Be open and say yes to stuff and meet up with people
Spend it all and take easy courses

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Take easy courses, some get fucked if not. Business courses in particular are easy - just like CBS courses

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people I have met and the amount of d-vitamins collected on hong kongs beaches. Learning about the conflict that has been there for some years. And the amount of asia I have been able to see while I was there

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Finding a sunscreen with less than PFS 50

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: GO!

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
